library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Yamaguchi et al. (2026) built a semi-mechanistic PK / receptor-occupancy (RO)
model of S-531011, a humanized anti-CCR8 IgG1 antibody in development for solid
tumors, to predict CCR8 occupancy in human tumor tissue, which the
first-in-human study does not measure. A mouse version of the same model was
compared with tumor RO measured in CT26.WT tumor-bearing human CCR8 knock-in
mice, the in vitro Kd was multiplied by 30 to match those data, and the refined
Kd was carried into the final human model. The paper therefore contributes two
model files that share one structure:

* `Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human` -- the final human model (Table 1 Human column,
  Data S1).
* `Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_mouse` -- the refined mouse model (Table 1 Mouse
  column).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human"))$reference`
* Description (human): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human"))$description`
* Description (mouse): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70332>

# Population

The human PK parameters were fitted to the mean serum concentrations of the
three participants in the 24 mg cohort (2-h IV infusion) of Part A-1 of the
first-in-human Phase 1b/2 study, which enrolled adults (18 years or older) with
locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors and ECOG performance status 0-1.
Part A-1 escalated S-531011 monotherapy at 8, 24, 80, 240, 800 and 1600 mg every
3 weeks (40 participants in total). No demographic table is reported. The
binding parameters come from in vitro KinExA and internalization assays, the
tumor-distribution parameters from a CT26.WT mouse study and the literature,
and the CCR8 expression levels and T-cell counts from published human data.

The mouse PK parameters were fitted to the mean serum concentrations of four
female BALB/c human CCR8 knock-in mice (10 weeks old, dosed 8 days after
subcutaneous CT26.WT implantation) given 5 mg/kg IV. Tumor RO was measured in a
separate group of 5 mice per dose and day at 0.05, 0.5 and 5 mg/kg.

```{r population}
readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human")()$population$notes
readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_mouse")()$population$species
```

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded next to each `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human.R` and
`..._mouse.R`. "Data S1" is the authors' SimBiology model report of the final
human model (`S-531011_PKRO_human_modified`), which lists every parameter,
initial assignment, reaction and ODE.

| Equation / parameter | Human | Mouse | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kel` (1/h) | 4.79e-3 | 0.0324 | Table 1; Table S5 |
| `k12` (1/h) | 6.95e-3 | 0.136 | Table 1; Table S5 |
| `k21` (1/h) | 5.75e-3 | 0.0907 | Table 1; Table S5 |
| `vc` (L) | 2.47 | 1.14e-3 | Table 1 (Vcen); Table S5 |
| `vp` (L) | 2.99 | 1.71e-3 | Table 1 (Vper); Table S5 |
| `vtumor` (L) | 0.01 | 1.70e-4 | Table 1 (Vtum); Methods |
| `pdist` | 0.61 | 0.61 | Results (tumor-to-serum ratio at 24 h); Data S1 #29 |
| `fint` | 0.55 | 0.55 | Methods; Data S1 #30 |
| `kon` (L/nmol/h) | 11.85 | 11.85 | Table 1; Table S4 |
| `kd` (nmol/L, in vitro) | 0.01862 | 0.01862 | Table S4 (18.62 pmol/L); Data S1 #31 |
| `fadj` | 30 | 30 | Results ("30 times the initial value"); Data S1 #70 |
| `thalf_cpx` (h) | 1.71 | 1.71 | Table S4; Data S1 #47 |
| `mw` (g/mol) | 148653.5 | 148653.5 | Data S1 #67 |
| CCR8 expression per Treg / Tconv / CD8 (central, peripheral, tumor) | 400 / 575 / 0; 1803 / 812 / 1274; 3573 / 906 / 1790 | -- | Data S1 #32-40 |
| `n_cd4_cen`, `n_cd8_cen` (cells/uL) | 861, 505 | -- | Data S1 #41-42 |
| `f_treg_cd4_cen`, `n_treg_tum`, `f_treg_cd4_tum`, `r_cd4_cd8_tum` | 0.07, 62.31 cells/mm^2, 0.189, 1.56 | -- | Data S1 #43-46 |
| `funit` (mm^3/mm^2), `dens` (uL/mm^3) | 0.707, 1 | -- | Data S1 #62-63 |
| Baseline CCR8, central / peripheral / tumor (nmol) | computed (1.987e-3 / 4.204e-3 / 1.980e-5) | 8.476e-7 / 5.791e-8 / 4.679e-7 | Table 1; Table S2-S3; Data S1 initial assignments 13-15 |
| `k13`, `k31` | computed (1.712e-5, 6.933e-3) | computed (0.01134, 0.1247) | Table S2; Table 1 |
| `koff = kd * fadj * kon` | computed (6.619) | computed (6.619) | Table S2; Data S1 initial assignment 2 |
| `kdeg = 0.693 / thalf_cpx`, `ksyn = kdeg * CCR8(0)` | computed | computed | Table S2, Table S4; Data S1 initial assignments 16-19 |
| IIV (30 percent CV on kel, Vc; 50 percent CV on kon, Pdist, fint, Kd, Thalf,CPX, Vtum) | yes | Kd only (50 percent CV) | Methods (Simulation); Figure S5 caption |
| ODEs for drug, CCR8, 1:1 and 1:2 complexes in three compartments | | | Table S1; Data S1 ODEs 1-12 |
| RO = 100 (1 - CCR8(t) / CCR8(0)) | | | Methods equations; Data S1 repeated assignments 1-3 |

# Derived constants against the authors' code

The human file computes the CCR8 baselines, `k13`, `k31`, `koff`, `kdeg` and the
synthesis rates from the primitive inputs, exactly as the SimBiology model does.
The typical values must equal the values Data S1 prints.

```{r derived}
mod_h <- readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human")
mod_h_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_h)
one <- rxode2::et(amt = 0, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(0)
der <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h_typ, one, returnType = "data.frame")[1, ]

data_s1 <- c(
  k13 = 1.7122e-05, k31 = 0.0069329, koff = 6.6194, kdeg = 0.40526,
  ccr8_cen_int = 0.0019873, ccr8_per_int = 0.0042044, ccr8_tum_int = 1.9803e-05,
  ksyn_cen = 0.00080538, ksyn_per = 0.0017039, ksyn_tum = 8.0256e-06
)
derived_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = names(data_s1),
  model = signif(unlist(der[names(data_s1)]), 5),
  data_s1 = data_s1
) |>
  mutate(rel_diff_pct = round(100 * (model - data_s1) / data_s1, 3))
derived_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Model" = model, "Data S1" = data_s1, "Difference (%)" = rel_diff_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value derived constants of the human model vs the SimBiology report (Data S1).")

# Deterministic: same inputs and formulas, so only print rounding separates them.
stopifnot(all(abs(derived_tab$rel_diff_pct) < 0.05))
```

# Human serum PK (Figure S2)

Figure S2 shows the two-compartment fit to the mean serum concentrations after
a single 24 mg dose infused over 2 h. Because the tumor volume is tiny relative
to Vc and Vp, the full PK/RO model reproduces the two-compartment curve.

```{r fig-s2}
ev_24 <- rxode2::et(amt = 24, dur = 2, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(sort(unique(c(seq(0, 504, by = 2), 1, 3, 5))))
pk24 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h_typ, ev_24, returnType = "data.frame")

# Observed means read by the maintainers from Figure S2 (open circles).
fig_s2_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~Cc,
  2, 9.6,
  3, 9.5,
  5, 9.1,
  24, 7.85,
  48, 5.65,
  72, 4.7,
  168, 2.6,
  336, 1.62,
  504, 1.12
)

ggplot(dplyr::filter(pk24, time > 0), aes(time / 24, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = fig_s2_obs, shape = 1, colour = "red", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the start of the infusion (day)", y = "Serum S-531011 (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S2B of Yamaguchi 2026 (24 mg, 2-h infusion). Points: digitised observed means."
  )

s2_chk <- fig_s2_obs |>
  mutate(pred = approx(pk24$time, pk24$Cc, xout = time)$y, pct_diff = 100 * (pred - Cc) / Cc)
s2_chk |>
  mutate(pred = signif(pred, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time, "Figure S2 observed mean (ug/mL)" = Cc,
    "Model (ug/mL)" = pred, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value serum concentrations vs the digitised Figure S2 means.")

# Deterministic typical-value curve vs digitised points: the fit is
# least-squares through these means, so a mis-transcribed volume or rate
# shifts the curve by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(s2_chk$pct_diff)) < 5, max(abs(s2_chk$pct_diff)) < 12)
```

## PKNCA on the 24 mg profile

The paper reports no NCA table. PKNCA is run on a simulated 24 mg cohort (with
the authors' simulation variability on kel and Vc) and the typical-value Cmax
is compared against the end-of-infusion mean read from Figure S2. The
simulated value is the median of individual Cmax values; with 30% variability
on Vc it sits a few percent below the typical-value Cmax (9.6 ug/mL, table
above).

```{r pknca}
mod_h_pk <- readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_human")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
ev_nca <- rxode2::et(amt = 24, dur = 2, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 420, 504)) |>
  rxode2::et(id = 1:100) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = "24 mg")
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h_pk, ev_nca, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")

conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_df,
  conc_df |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)
dose_df <- ev_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(evid != 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 504, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "24 mg", cmax = 9.6)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated NCA (median of 100 virtual participants) vs the Figure S2 end-of-infusion mean. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

# Final human model: tumor RO time course (Figure 2)

The authors simulated 8, 24, 80, 240, 800 and 1600 mg every 3 weeks with 1-h
infusions (Data S1 repeat doses: four infusions, at 0, 504, 1008 and 1512 h)
with their assumed between-subject variability. 200 virtual participants are
simulated per dose here.

```{r fig2-sim}
doses <- c(8, 24, 80, 240, 800, 1600)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1512, by = 6), 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 503.99, 1007.99, 1511.99)))

make_cohort <- function(dose, n, id_offset) {
  rxode2::et(amt = dose, dur = 1, ii = 504, addl = 3, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_times) |>
    rxode2::et(id = id_offset + seq_len(n)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(dose_mg = dose)
}
events_q3w <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
  make_cohort(doses[i], n = 200, id_offset = (i - 1) * 200)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_q3w[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
sim_q3w <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, events_q3w, keep = "dose_mg", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r fig2-plot}
sim_q3w |>
  group_by(dose_mg, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.025), med = median(ro_tumor), hi = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(dose = factor(paste(dose_mg, "mg"), levels = paste(doses, "mg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:9) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the start of the 1st infusion (week)", y = "Receptor occupancy in tumor (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yamaguchi 2026: median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles."
  )
```

The paper states that the tumor RO at 1512 h (trough after the third dose) of
80 mg stays above 90%.

```{r ro-80mg}
trough_80 <- sim_q3w |> dplyr::filter(dose_mg == 80, time == 1511.99)
c(median = median(trough_80$ro_tumor), p2.5 = unname(quantile(trough_80$ro_tumor, 0.025)))
# Results: RO at 1512 h after 80 mg 'could be maintained at more than 90%'.
# The median sits near 98 and the 2.5th percentile near 91; the paper's claim
# is about the central prediction, so only the median is asserted.
stopifnot(median(trough_80$ro_tumor) > 90)
```

# Cycle 2 pre-dose RO, base and conservative Pdist (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows the RO in tumor just before the second dose (C2D1 pre, 504 h)
for the final model and for the conservative condition in which Pdist is one
tenth of its final-model value. The medians were read by the maintainers from
Figure 3.

```{r fig3}
mod_h_cons <- mod_h |> rxode2::ini(lpdist = log(0.061))
events_c2 <- events_q3w |> dplyr::filter(evid != 0 | time == 503.99)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
c2_base <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h, events_c2, keep = "dose_mg", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(scenario = "Base")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
c2_cons <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_h_cons, events_c2, keep = "dose_mg", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(scenario = "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)")

c2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(c2_base, c2_cons) |>
  group_by(scenario, dose_mg) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.025), med = median(ro_tumor), hi = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(c2, aes(factor(dose_mg), med)) +
  geom_crossbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "lightblue", colour = "blue", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose level (mg)", y = "RO in tumor at C2D1 pre (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Yamaguchi 2026: median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles."
  )

fig3_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~dose_mg, ~fig_median,
  "Base", 8, 77.5,
  "Base", 24, 91.8,
  "Base", 80, 97.5,
  "Base", 240, 99.0,
  "Base", 800, 99.8,
  "Base", 1600, 100,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 8, 22.5,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 24, 49.0,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 80, 78.0,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 240, 91.8,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 800, 97.5,
  "Conservative (1/10 Pdist)", 1600, 98.8
)

# Typical-value prediction at 503.99 h for each scenario and dose.
ev_typ <- function(dose) {
  rxode2::et(amt = dose, dur = 1, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(503.99)
}
typ_c2 <- function(m, dose) {
  utils::tail(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(m), ev_typ(dose), returnType = "data.frame")$ro_tumor, 1)
}
fig3_cmp <- fig3_digitised |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(typical = typ_c2(if (scenario == "Base") mod_h else mod_h_cons, dose_mg)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(c2 |> dplyr::select(scenario, dose_mg, sim_median = med), by = c("scenario", "dose_mg")) |>
  mutate(diff_typical = typical - fig_median)

fig3_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(typical, sim_median, diff_typical), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Dose (mg)" = dose_mg, "Figure 3 median" = fig_median,
    "Typical value" = typical, "Simulated median" = sim_median, "Typical - Figure (RO points)" = diff_typical
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "RO in tumor at C2D1 pre-dose (%): digitised Figure 3 medians vs the packaged model.")

# Deterministic typical value vs digitised medians: observed agreement is
# within 1 RO point; a wrong Kd adjustment, k13/k31 or CCR8 baseline moves
# the low-dose values by tens of points.
stopifnot(max(abs(fig3_cmp$diff_typical)) < 3)
```

# Mouse model (Figures S1 and S5)

The mouse model is dosed in mg. The paper doses in mg/kg and does not state the
body weight it used; the predicted curve of Figure S1 (5 mg/kg) starts at about
110 ug/mL in a 1.14 mL central volume, i.e. an absolute dose of about 0.125 mg,
so the maintainers use 25 g per mouse throughout.

```{r mouse-pk}
mod_m <- readModelDb("Yamaguchi_2026_s531011_mouse")
mod_m_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_m)
bw_kg <- 0.025

ev_m5 <- rxode2::et(amt = 5 * bw_kg, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(seq(0, 168, by = 1))
pk_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m_typ, ev_m5, returnType = "data.frame")

# Observed means read by the maintainers from Figure S1 (open circles).
fig_s1_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~Cc,
  0.25, 105,
  6, 51,
  24, 26.5,
  96, 13,
  168, 4.8
)
ggplot(dplyr::filter(pk_m, time > 0), aes(time / 24, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = fig_s1_obs, shape = 1, colour = "red", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (day)", y = "Serum S-531011 (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S1B of Yamaguchi 2026 (mouse, 5 mg/kg, 25 g body weight assumed)."
  )
s1_chk <- fig_s1_obs |>
  mutate(pred = approx(pk_m$time, pk_m$Cc, xout = time)$y, pct_diff = 100 * (pred - Cc) / Cc)
s1_chk |>
  mutate(pred = signif(pred, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Figure S1 mean (ug/mL)" = Cc, "Model (ug/mL)" = pred, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value mouse serum concentrations vs digitised Figure S1 means.")
stopifnot(abs(median(s1_chk$pct_diff)) < 10)
```

Figure S5 shows the tumor RO of the refined mouse model with a 50% CV on Kd
(the authors used 500 animals; 200 per dose here), against the adjusted
observed RO at 24 h.

```{r mouse-ro}
mouse_doses <- c(0.05, 0.5, 5)
m_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 2), 0.25, 0.5, 1, 10)))
events_m <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mouse_doses), function(i) {
  rxode2::et(amt = mouse_doses[i] * bw_kg, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(m_times) |>
    rxode2::et(id = (i - 1) * 200 + seq_len(200)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(dose_mgkg = mouse_doses[i])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_m[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
sim_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m, events_m, keep = "dose_mgkg", returnType = "data.frame")

sum_m <- sim_m |>
  group_by(dose_mgkg, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.025), mean = mean(ro_tumor), hi = quantile(ro_tumor, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(dose = factor(paste(dose_mgkg, "mg/kg"), levels = paste(mouse_doses, "mg/kg")))

ggplot(sum_m, aes(time, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, by = 24)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 110)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Receptor occupancy in tumor (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S5 of Yamaguchi 2026: mean and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles."
  )

# Mean simulated RO at 168 h read by the maintainers from Figure S5.
fig_s5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_mgkg, ~fig_mean_168,
  0.05, 28.5,
  0.5, 79.0,
  5, 97.3
)
s5_cmp <- fig_s5 |>
  mutate(typical = sapply(dose_mgkg, function(d) {
    e <- rxode2::et(amt = d * bw_kg, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(168)
    utils::tail(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m_typ, e, returnType = "data.frame")$ro_tumor, 1)
  })) |>
  left_join(sum_m |> dplyr::filter(time == 168) |> dplyr::select(dose_mgkg, sim_mean = mean), by = "dose_mgkg")
s5_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(typical, sim_mean), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose_mgkg, "Figure S5 mean at 168 h" = fig_mean_168,
    "Typical value" = typical, "Simulated mean" = sim_mean
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mouse tumor RO at 168 h (%): digitised Figure S5 vs the packaged model.")
# Deterministic typical value; observed agreement is within 1 RO point at
# 0.5 and 5 mg/kg and within 1 point at 0.05 mg/kg (where the Kd spread
# makes the mean sit about 1 point above the typical value).
stopifnot(max(abs(s5_cmp$typical - s5_cmp$fig_mean_168)) < 5)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Kd adjustment.** Table 1 prints the optimized koff as 6.621 1/h; the
  authors' SimBiology report (Data S1) computes `koff = Kd x Fadj x kon` =
  0.01862 x 30 x 11.85 = 6.6194 1/h, and that is what both files use. The
  difference is rounding in Table 1.
- **ln 2.** The SimBiology code uses `ln2 = 0.693` for `Tdist` and `kdeg`;
  the files keep that constant, so `kdeg` = 0.40526 1/h exactly as in Data S1
  (Table 1 prints 0.4053).
- **Primitive inputs from the model code.** The human CCR8 expression levels,
  T-cell counts, `funit` and the molecular weight appear only in Data S1, not
  in the article tables; the human file takes them from there and computes the
  CCR8 baselines, which reproduce the Table 1 amounts. The mouse file uses the
  Table 1 baseline CCR8 amounts directly because the mouse expression inputs
  (CCR8 per CCR8-positive CD4 T cell, fraction of CCR8-positive CD4 T cells) are
  not tabulated.
- **Between-subject variability.** The Methods give "30% (coefficient of
  variation; CV)" for kel and Vc and "50%" for kon, Pdist, fint, Kd,
  Thalf,CPX and Vtum. They are encoded as log-normal with variance
  log(1 + CV^2). The mouse Figure S5 percentiles are reproduced closely with
  this reading. With a 50% CV, fint exceeds 1 in roughly one simulated subject
  in ten; the source does not say whether the authors truncated it, so no
  truncation is applied.
- **IIV on Vc and Vtum propagates into the CCR8 baselines, k13 and k31**, because
  the human file computes them from the individual volumes as SimBiology's
  initial assignments do.
- **Residual error.** None in the source (the PK parameters were fitted to mean
  concentrations and the RO model is a simulation model); `propSd` is set to
  zero.
- **Dosing in mg.** The SimBiology model doses in nmol (for example 8 mg as
  53.82 nmol). The packaged models take doses in mg and convert with the
  molecular weight (1 mg = 1e6 / 148653.5 nmol); drug states are in mg and
  CCR8 and complex states in nmol.
- **Infusion duration.** The simulations, like the authors', use 1-h infusions
  for every cycle; in the clinical study the first infusion lasted 2 h, which
  is what the Figure S2 replication uses.
- **Mouse body weight.** Not reported; 25 g, back-calculated from the start of
  the Figure S1 predicted curve, is used to convert mg/kg to mg.
- **Fadj in the mouse file** is left estimable (it is the parameter the
  authors selected against mouse tumor RO); in the human file it is carried as
  a constant.
- **Pdist conservative scenarios** (1/3 and 1/10 of 0.61, Figures S8, S9 and
  3) are obtained by changing `lpdist` with `rxode2::ini()`, as shown above.
- No erratum for the article was found as of 2026-11-17.
